decision: held: re-decided with the open 34555168 full text (PMC8970830) per Dr. Pham's fifth ruling; it is a non-pooled review whose bowel-function findings are mixed (transit time mostly unchanged, one positive scFOS trial; flatulence increased in 19 of 37 studies), so it cannot carry credit alone; the meta-analyses that could (35833477 Crit Rev Food Sci Nutr 2023, closed; 38309832 Am J Clin Nutr 2024, OpenAlex bronze copy but publisher returned only an HTML landing page) remain unread in full
summary: The 2022 Adv Nutr review (full text) summarizes 78 healthy-adult trials at about 2.5-50 g/day with mixed, preparation-dependent laxation and microbiota results, but pools nothing; it is recorded as a completed no-credit context. The chicory-fructan meta-analysis (abstract: 50 studies, Bifidobacterium SMD 0.83, bowel-function benefit in healthy subjects) is the natural credit source but could not be verified from full text, so the record stays held under Dr. Pham's A079 source-content hold.

identity.name: Inulin, oligofructose and short-chain fructooligosaccharides; chemical chain length and food matrix differ.

population.description: 78 publications of human clinical trials in healthy adults (45 on fecal microbiota/metabolites plus laxation, glucose, lipid, mineral, satiety, inflammation and body-composition outcomes).

study_contexts.study_design: Qualitative systematic review (searched February 2021) of human clinical trials of inulin-type fructans in healthy adults; no pooled meta-analysis.

outcomes.name: Some microbiota and intestinal-function changes reported; selected metabolic or absorption outcomes differ by trial.

limitations: Microbial abundance is not automatically a patient-important benefit.
Physicochemical characterization and direct chain-length comparisons are often lacking; do not manufacture material equivalence.

Included-study identifiers are now bound to this source's actual included-study rows/explicit inclusion references (Tables tbl1,tbl2,tbl3,tbl4,tbl5,tbl6,tbl7,tbl8 explicit included-study row citations), with live NIH title/content identity checks. They are publication pointers, not independent-cohort counts, per-primary-study scoring approvals, preparation equivalence or new efficacy evidence. Exact unindexed source citations remain retained; no missing PMID is invented.

3 included source citations have no printed PubMed identifier in this primary source; their exact citations are retained in the source-table receipt. This is a documented identifier limitation, not a fabricated identifier or an extra independent trial.

Full text re-read 2026-10-28 (PMC8970830): transit time showed no change versus control in most trials, with one scFOS trial (6.4 g/d) accelerating colonic transit; 19 of 37 studies reported increased flatulence; one inulin trial (11 g/d) lowered serum zonulin.

No credit from this source: it is a qualitative systematic review without pooled estimates, so it does not meet the RCT/meta-analysis rule; findings are mixed by chain length and preparation (the record notes eleven positive and nine null stool-frequency studies). Support from General Mills is disclosed.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

dose.administration_frequency: Trial-specific daily intake, often escalated over the first weeks (Tables 1-8).
dosage_forms: oral supplementation and fortified foods (trial-specific preparations)
co_therapies: Food matrices, habitual diet and individual baseline microbiota differ.
dose.reported_regimen: Trial ITF dosages roughly 2.5-50 g/day (most 5-20 g/day; some escalation protocols) for 1-96 weeks across Tables 1-8; delivered as supplements or in foods such as cereal, bars, biscuits and yogurt.

normalization.basis: A heterogeneous synthesis has no single assigned-arm dose. Descriptive regimens do not create an intake recommendation, equivalent preparation or efficacy threshold.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC8970830): Methods (search, selection), Results (78 publications), Tables 1-8 (ITF type, DP, dosage g/d, duration, population).
